title: Workflows: convert canvas workflows back to graphs and save them
brief:
Desktop app (folder desktop/). desktop/src/services/workflowApi.ts already has `graphToCompiler(id, g: Graph): CompilerWorkflow` (read it first). It adds a synthetic node {id:'start', type:'start'} with an edge to g.start, maps each graph node to a CompilerNode whose data = { agent: <graph node type>, instruction: <name or type>, params }, maps position [x,y] to {x,y}, and puts non-'out' ports on edges as data.when.
1. Add and export the exact inverse `compilerToGraph(w: CompilerWorkflow, base?: Graph): Graph`: drop the 'start' node; g.start = target of the edge whose source is 'start' (fallback: base?.start or the first remaining node id); each other node -> { id, type: String(data.agent), name: data.instruction if it differs from data.agent, params: data.params if non-empty, position: [x, y] rounded to integers if present }; each edge not from 'start' -> { from: source, to: target, port: data.when } (omit port when there is no data.when). name = w.name, description = w.description ?? base?.description. Round-trip property: compilerToGraph(graphToCompiler(id, g)) deep-equals g for graphs whose names differ from their types and whose params are non-empty (positions integer).
2. Change saveUserWorkflow(workflow: CompilerWorkflow): PUT `${SERVER_BASE}/api/workflows/user/${encodeURIComponent(workflow.id)}` with body { graph: compilerToGraph(workflow) } (keep using serverFetch). Response JSON is { status: 'saved' | 'invalid', problems: string[] }: if status is 'invalid' throw Error('Workflow is invalid: ' + problems.join('; ')); if !res.ok throw the parsed error. Keep the same exported signature. Leave deleteUserWorkflow throwing as now. listWorkflowItems should now return readOnly: false.
3. Add tests to desktop/src/services/workflowApi.test.ts (keep the existing ones): round trip on a graph with a loop edge with port 'retry', a 'human.approval' node, params and positions; and start detection.

title: Workflows: edit node positions and parameters in the graph view and save
brief:
Desktop app (React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind + @xyflow/react, folder desktop/). desktop/src/components/SmurfGraphView.tsx is a read-only @xyflow/react view of a `CompilerWorkflow` (from desktop/src/services/workflowFormat.ts), shown by desktop/src/components/WorkflowOrchestration.tsx for workflows the classic canvas cannot edit. desktop/src/services/workflowApi.ts exports `saveUserWorkflow(workflow: CompilerWorkflow): Promise<void>` (PUT to the server, throws 'Workflow is invalid: ...' with the engine's validation problems).
The server also has GET /api/nodes returning the node registry: `{ type: string; label: string; group: string; description: string; ports: string[]; params: { name: string; type: 'string'|'number'|'boolean'|'select'; default?: unknown; options?: string[]; description: string }[] }[]` (fetch it with `serverJson` from desktop/src/services/serverUrl.ts, fallback []).
1. Create desktop/src/components/NodeParamsForm.tsx exporting `NodeParamsForm({ spec, value, onChange })` where spec is the param list of one node type and value is Record<string, unknown>: render one labelled control per param (text input for string, number input for number, checkbox for boolean, <select> for select with its options), showing the description as small help text and the default as placeholder. Export a pure helper `coerceParam(spec, raw: string | boolean): unknown` (number -> Number or undefined when empty, boolean -> boolean, others -> string; empty string -> undefined).
2. Create desktop/src/components/NodeParamsForm.test.tsx (vitest) testing coerceParam.
3. In SmurfGraphView.tsx add an optional `onSave?: (w: CompilerWorkflow) => Promise<void>` prop. When onSave is given: nodes are draggable (keep positions in component state), clicking a node selects it and shows a side panel (right side, ~280px) with the node id, its type (data.agent), a Name field bound to data.instruction, and <NodeParamsForm> for data.params using the registry entry whose type equals data.agent (no form if not found). A toolbar above the graph has 'Save' (disabled until something changed) and 'Reset' buttons; Save builds the updated CompilerWorkflow (new positions, names, params) and awaits onSave, then shows 'Saved' or the error message (e.g. the server's validation problems) in a small status line. Without onSave the view stays read-only exactly as today. Keep the existing `layoutOrder` export and its tests.
4. In WorkflowOrchestration.tsx pass `onSave={async (w) => { await saveUserWorkflow(w); <refresh the workflow list the way the file already does after saving, if easy> }}` to SmurfGraphView. Smallest possible change there.
